A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VSD work. All 19 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v4, including their appendices, are readable. Text extraction and visual inspection support matching the methods, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM and multimodal decoding experiments, acceptance-path diagnostics, component ablations and appendix results for the KL variant.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds a batch-size experiment in Table 5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the proposal-and-correction procedure, oracle, ARW and CAR gradient formulas. The draft-tree procedure and top-10 KL variant also remain. Replacing 'MCMC' with 'Monte Carlo' changes the description, while the revised optimality analysis does not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training corpora and evaluations on MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, VQAv2, AI2D, SQA Image, ChartQA, TextVQA and Hallusion. The added batching experiment changes execution settings within retained tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their comparator membership, including GRIFFIN/HASS in Table 3 and the multimodal baselines in Table 2. The new batching experiment reuses EAGLE-3. The appendix VSD (KL) comparison already appears in v1.

E3.justification: v4 adds decoding batch sizes 4 and 8 at temperatures 0 and 1 on the retained LLM benchmarks, supplementing batch-size-1 evaluation. Table 3 also relabels its target from LLaMA-3-Instruct-8B to LLaMA-3.1-Instruct-8B while retaining the scores and older name in surrounding text; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 5 and Section 5.2 test whether VSD's gains persist under larger decoding batches. Existing analyses of proposal count, ARW, CAR and the KL variant are retained. This is a focused extension of the sensitivity evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose averaging over three independent runs in the experimental appendices. v4 adds no seed identities, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests or revised uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing table scores are retained, including v1 Table 5, now v4 Table 7. New Table 5 reports average speedup ratios of 2.63 versus 2.83 at batch size 4 and 1.67 versus 1.81 at batch size 8, for EAGLE-3 versus EAGLE-3+VSD at temperature 0. Section 5.1 also adds model-specific greedy-acceptance figures.

T1.justification: v1's Theorem 2 asserts optimality for the original VSD objective. v4 recasts this as Theorem 3 for an EM-step surrogate whose verification probabilities are fixed using the preceding draft distribution, with explicit full-support assumptions and a revised proof in Appendix C.3. This substantially changes the guarantee's scope. The KL-only comparison promoted to Theorem 2 already existed in v1 Appendix B.3.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of verification-aware variational draft training, EM optimization with ARW/CAR, lossless decoding and improved efficiency across LLMs and MLLMs. The conclusion's added theoretical claim repeats claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations involving draft–target mismatch, output horizon, posterior entropy and batching. The proposal-count and modality limitations remain. The new 70B interpretation contains inconsistencies: it names LLaMA-3.1-70B and uses 5.7% in an MT-Bench comparison, whereas Table 1 identifies LLaMA-3.3-70B and reports 5.7% as its temperature-1 cross-task average.

D1.justification: Section 5 changes the one/two-GPU statement from draft training to experiment execution and clarifies that baseline hardware includes RTX PRO 6000 or L-40S. These refine previously inconsistent hardware descriptions. Detailed training configurations and resource-access information remain unchanged in v1 Appendix E and v4 Appendix F.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning of VSD as complementary to existing speculative decoding methods remain. EAGLE-3's reference changes from a 2025 preprint to publication metadata, representing the same cited work.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites parts of the results discussion, consistently replaces MCMC terminology, adds a notation appendix and acknowledgements, and reorganizes the theoretical exposition. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain, making this a localized revision rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 adds the batch-size table and notation table, removes Table 3's model column while moving model identification into its caption, and introduces running headers and associated reflow. Figure 1 and the principal benchmark displays remain substantially unchanged; the existing appendix result table is renumbered.

improvement.justification: The revised optimality theorem makes the fixed-verifier condition explicit, addressing an important ambiguity in v1, and Table 5 adds useful evidence about batching robustness. These provide a limited net improvement in precision and empirical support. Benefits are tempered by the new 70B discussion's mismatch with Table 1 and retained claims of guaranteed speedup that exceed what the lower-bound comparisons establish.
